strengths: Comprehensive and balanced contribution addressing both attack and defense: proposes a principled geometric steganographic scheme and investigates interpretability-based detection methods.
Clear conceptual formalization of payload recoverability, decoupling the token-to-bucket inference difficulty from the bucket-to-secret decoding difficulty.

Solid theoretical analysis providing explicit lower bounds on KL divergence (Theorem 7.1) and perplexity (Theorem 7.2), rigorously explaining why output-level distributional steganalysis fails against fine-tuned steganography.

Thorough empirical evaluation across multiple model architectures (Llama-3.1-8B, Ministral-8B, Llama-3.3-70B), fine-tuning modalities (LoRA vs. Full FT), mixed-motive training regimes, out-of-distribution prompts, decoding temperature variations, and retokenization dynamics.

Convincing demonstration of mechanistic detection via linear probes (bit classification and embedding regression) that remains robust even when the secret is deliberately masked via XOR control to prevent text decoding.
weaknesses: The evaluated secret capacity is limited to 4 characters (32 bits), leaving scalability to larger, arbitrary payload sizes largely uncharacterized empirically.
Detection requires white-box or gray-box access to intermediate layer representations, restricting defense applicability in API-only or black-box deployment contexts.

Embedding-based character encoding relies on a collision-free hyperplane search that scales poorly to larger character sets/alphabets, although ASCII encoding with embedding bucketing mitigates this in practice.

strengths: Comprehensive dual contribution: The paper thoughtfully investigates both the attack vector (designing embedding-geometry based steganography that resists output reverse-engineering) and the defense side (demonstrating mechanistic interpretability as a viable detection mechanism).

Formalization of payload recoverability: Introducing classifier-based formal metrics for bucket recoverability (R_bucket) and secret recoverability (R_secret) fills an important gap in evaluating the security of LLM covert channels beyond standard perceptual fluency.

Rigorous and extensive empirical evaluation: Experiments span multiple model families (Llama 3.1, Ministral) and scales (8B to 70B), full fine-tuning vs. LoRA, out-of-distribution prompt transfer, standard NLP capability benchmarks (MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag, WinoGrande), sampling temperatures, and tokenizer re-encoding stability.

Methodological rigor with the XOR control: The secret-conditioned XOR control in Section 7.5 is an elegant experimental design that cleanly isolates internal representation changes from output-side decodability.

Practical considerations addressed: The mixed-motive training study realistically addresses the capability degradation seen in single-objective steganographic training, making the threat model and defense evaluation significantly more grounded.
weaknesses: Stylized theoretical assumptions: The bounds in Theorems 7.1 and 7.2 rely on idealized assumptions (e.g., peaky base model distribution where top mass is concentrated on one or two tokens, or deterministic top token assumption in the PPL lower bound) that simplify real-world multi-token autoregressive LM dynamics.

Narrow payload scope in experiments: All empirical studies encode short 4-letter secrets (32 bits). While Appendix I.1 acknowledges this limitation, evaluating whether the attack remains fluent and whether probes remain accurate as payload lengths scale to realistic exfiltration targets (e.g., cryptographic keys, long PII) would significantly strengthen the empirical claims.

Defender threat model assumptions for probing: Probing requires white-box or gray-box access to activations as well as synthetic prompts with suspected secret formats to generate supervision for training the probes. The paper does not thoroughly evaluate how robust probe-based detection is against an adversary who uses subtle or variable prompt triggers.

strengths: Comprehensive and balanced contribution addressing both attack capabilities and defensive detection in training-time LLM steganography.

Rigorous formalization of payload recoverability (Definition 3.1) separating token-to-bucket and bucket-to-secret inference difficulty, clearly identifying the structural reversibility limitation of prior work like TrojanStego.

Technically grounded method: using random hyperplanes in embedding space provides a key-dependent bucketing mechanism that naturally aligns with semantic geometry, enhancing training learnability while dramatically reducing unauthorized keyless recovery.

Solid theoretical contributions (Theorems 7.1 and 7.2) showing that steganographic distribution shifts (KL divergence and perplexity) can remain well within normal fine-tuning variations, fundamentally justifying the shift toward internal mechanistic steganalysis.

Extensive empirical evaluation across multiple model architectures (Llama-3.1-8B, Ministral-8B, Llama-3.3-70B), fine-tuning paradigms (Full FT vs. LoRA), downstream capability benchmarks (MMLU, ARC-C, HellaSwag, WinoGrande), and practical channel noise (temperature variation and tokenizer retokenization).
weaknesses: The empirical experiments are primarily restricted to fixed-length 4-character secrets (32 bits); extending this to larger, variable-length payloads (e.g., long confidential texts, arbitrary byte sequences) remains unverified and may incur harsher capability degradation.

The linear probe defense relies on white-box/gray-box activation access, rendering it inapplicable to black-box API monitoring or third-party downstream consumers lacking weight/activation visibility.

Detection practicality in deployment is not fully resolved: while probes achieve high separation between base and fine-tuned models on test sets, the paper does not quantify end-to-end false positive rates when scanning large volumes of heterogeneous benign prompts.

The attack setting assumes the prompt explicitly contains a trigger prefix and plaintext secret (e.g., 'Secret: abcd'), which restricts the realistic threat model to specific workflows where sensitive context is already supplied in a structured format.

strengths: Clear conceptual formalization: The paper formalizes payload recoverability along two distinct axes (token-to-bucket inference difficulty and bucket-to-secret decoding difficulty), providing a principled diagnostic for assessing whether an analyst without the key can reconstruct exfiltrated data.

Technically grounded attack design: Replacing arbitrary heuristics (e.g., parity rules) with random hyperplane projections in the token embedding space aligns bucket structures with the model's learned geometry, yielding improved exact secret recovery (e.g., up to +123% on Llama-70B LoRA) while reducing reverse-engineering feasibility.

Insightful analysis of steganalysis limits: The paper provides theoretical bounds on KL divergence and perplexity, demonstrating analytically and empirically why standard distributional steganalysis is inadequate for detecting fine-tuning-based covert channels.

Effective use of internal representations: The proposed mechanistic interpretability defense demonstrates that even when exfiltrated payloads are mathematically unrecoverable from surface text (via XOR controls), steganographic fine-tuning leaves detectable linear signatures in late-layer activations across out-of-distribution prompts.
weaknesses: Defender assumptions in probe training: The detection framework relies on training linear probes or ridge regressors on activations corresponding to known secrets (or PCA-reduced letter embeddings). In realistic deployment auditing, a defender may suspect exfiltration but lack labeled pairs of (prompts, true secrets, activations) to train these supervisory probes.

Sample size for text quality evaluation: As detailed in Appendix E, text quality metrics (coherence and stability) are evaluated on only 10 prompts per configuration, and KL divergence on 20 prompts. A larger, more diverse benchmark would provide stronger statistical confidence regarding generation degradation.

Rigidity of secret prompt framing: Steganographic encoding is triggered via rigid, explicit prompt keys (e.g., 'Secret: abcd' or 'Key: abcd'). It remains unclear whether the covert channel functions or can be similarly probed if secrets are subtly embedded in free-form context without explicit delimiter tokens.

Simplifying assumptions in theoretical bounds: Theorems 7.1 and 7.2 rely on specific stylized assumptions (e.g., uniform target distribution across buckets, stylized probability masses) that serve as proof-of-concept bounds rather than tight operational bounds under complex next-token entropy profiles.

strengths: The paper provides a clear and conceptually grounded formalization of payload recoverability, decoupling the inference of buckets from tokens (R_bucket) and the extraction of secrets from buckets (R_secret).

Replacing arbitrary parity and ASCII mappings with embedding-space hyperplane partitioning is an elegant, well-motivated approach that aligns directly with the underlying geometry of LLM representations.

The theoretical bounds on minimal KL divergence (Theorem 7.1) and perplexity (Theorem 7.2) nicely formalize why standard output-level distributional steganalysis fails to detect fine-tuned covert channels under expected training drift.

The dual evaluation of both attack improvements (higher transmission accuracy and lower recoverability) and mechanistic defenses (linear probes and ridge regression on activations across layers) provides a balanced and thorough safety perspective.

Experiments cover multiple contemporary open-weight model architectures (Llama-3.1-8B, Ministral-8B, Llama-3.3-70B), full fine-tuning vs. LoRA, in-distribution and out-of-distribution prompts, and text fluency metrics.
weaknesses: The practical threat model for the probe-based defense needs further clarification: training the linear probes requires ground-truth labels (either target bits or secret embeddings), which implicitly assumes the auditor knows the secret structure or can generate prompt-secret pairs to test the model.

Detection is evaluated via raw probe metrics (bit accuracy and cosine similarity) rather than as an end-to-end statistical detection framework with formal detection thresholds, false positive rates, or AUROC against benign fine-tuned models.

The performance gains of embedding-based bucketing and encoding are mixed on fully fine-tuned models (e.g., Ministral full fine-tuning in Table 1 shows neutral or decreased exact match rates compared to baseline ASCII+Parity), suggesting the advantages are most pronounced under parameter-efficient regimes like LoRA.

strengths: Clear and formal formulation of payload recoverability along two complementary axes (token-to-bucket inference and bucket-to-secret decoding), highlighting fundamental vulnerabilities in previous heuristic schemes like TrojanStego.

Well-motivated attack design using random hyperplanes in token embedding space, which harmonizes with the geometry of learned representations and improves fine-tuning learning efficiency and exact match rate across multiple architectures (Llama-8B, Ministral-8B, Llama-70B).

Sound theoretical contributions, including derivation of lower bounds on KL divergence and perplexity under argmax-promotion steganographic constraints, explaining why distribution-divergence steganalysis fails against fine-tuned models.

Insightful mechanistic defense: demonstrating that internal representations in later layers leak steganographic activity via linear probes and embedding regression, validated even under a non-decodable XOR-masking control.
weaknesses: The defense evaluation assumes the defender has internal activation access (white-box / gray-box) and knows or can format queries with candidate secret triggers, which may not readily translate to passive black-box auditing or covert triggers.

While embedding recovery cosine similarities are consistently higher in fine-tuned models than in base models, the absolute values remain modest (~0.4–0.5 vs. ~0.25–0.35 baseline), and bit-level probe detection struggles under the XOR-masking control (succeeding in only 3 of 8 configurations).
